subject.title: fix(egress): keep replaced egress sessions dead across restarts and revocation

question: Should this PR land with the deliberate first-rollout egress reconnect behavior and the documented 256-session tombstone limit, or should rollout compatibility and durable server-bound identity be tightened first?
rationale: The patch improves a real stale-session takeover path, but it intentionally trades ambiguous restored sessions for disconnects and retains a bounded security residual that cannot be resolved mechanically without choosing the permanent protocol and upgrade policy.

options.title: Land with explicit rollout acceptance
options.body: Accept the reconnect-on-ambiguous-restore behavior and tracked 256-entry residual after real Worker runtime proof confirms the normal restart and revocation paths.

options.title: Add a compatibility rollout path
options.body: Preserve or migrate enough pre-existing session state to avoid closing legitimate restored sockets during the first deployment, while still refusing proven tombstoned sessions.

options.title: Pause for protocol identity design
options.body: Defer this hardening until a server-bound session identity removes the FIFO residual without relying on retained tombstone history.

recommendation.title: Land with explicit rollout acceptance
recommendation.body: Accept the reconnect-on-ambiguous-restore behavior and tracked 256-entry residual after real Worker runtime proof confirms the normal restart and revocation paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest direct history across the proposed coordinator mechanism and the previously merged egress replacement fixes.
